source.title: The Implicit and Explicit Regularization Effects of Dropout
source.authors: Colin Wei; S. Kakade; Tengyu Ma

page_placements.theme: Dropout, masking and normalization interact with the training recipe

record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally tests dropout’s effects on validation performance and whether explicit and implicit regularizers can reproduce them, using language-model perplexity rather than the claim versions’ classification settings.
record.gate_note: Results concern language modeling and validation perplexity. The paper does not test any listed version’s specified behavior. Figure-only comparisons are not separately extracted where tables report validation perplexities.
record.test_reason: The study tests dropout mechanisms and replacement regularizers in recurrent and Transformer language models using validation perplexity. These results do not test V6's fully connected and convolutional classifiers. It holds data minibatch size fixed while varying dropout-mask samples, so it does not test V5 either.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors identify entangled explicit regularization from the expected objective and implicit regularization from stochastic updates, derive analytical approximations, and show that their combination replaces dropout in the tested LSTMs. On full WikiText-103, the implicit benefit disappears and the explicit regularizer alone approaches Transformer-XL dropout performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies dropout regularization in LSTMs, Transformer-XL and QRNN language models; it varies the number of sampled dropout masks and tests derived replacement regularizers, rather than the claim versions’ image-classification settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The implicit effect varies with dataset size: it appears on Penn Treebank, Wikitext-2 and downsampled WikiText-103, while it disappears on full WikiText-103 for Transformer-XL and QRNN.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard dropout improves validation perplexity relative to no regularization: 73.76 versus 122.16 on Penn Treebank, 90.97 versus 144.12 on WikiText-2, and 23.39 versus 29.45 for Transformer-XL on full WikiText-103.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout improves held-out perplexity in these recurrent and Transformer language-model settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Averaging more dropout masks worsens LSTM validation perplexity on Penn Treebank and WikiText-2. The penalty is smaller on downsampled WikiText-103 and disappears on full WikiText-103 for Transformer-XL and QRNN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout update noise can provide implicit regularization in language models, with its importance depending on dataset size in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Derived noise restores standard-dropout performance, and combined analytical regularizers match or improve its validation perplexity on the two LSTM datasets. The explicit regularizer alone approaches dropout on full WikiText-103.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Analytical explicit and implicit regularizers can reproduce dropout performance in the tested language models.

record.problems: The paper reports best validation perplexity values without uncertainty estimates. Several comparisons are presented in figures; the text does not provide exact values for those plots. The experiments are language-modeling tasks, so they do not directly establish classifier-specific versions.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying classifier-version rows were reported. Figure-only epoch curves and additional tuned variants in Section 5.2 were not separately extracted because the tables provide the comparable principal validation results; Table 1’s tuned variants are also represented only where the corresponding reported value is a distinct table result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy with matched architectures and recipes.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Data-batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects in fully connected and convolutional classifiers, very small training sets, excessive dropout, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness ranking generalization gaps relative to norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numerical values match the supplied tables. States are assessed against the listed versions, so unlinked rows receive cannot_determine. The study is relevant background but tests none of V1–V8; its T2 classification should therefore be removed. Stability regularization and its theoretical bound do not test V7's empirical sharpness-ranking claim.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
The version specifies fully connected and convolutional classifiers, small training sets, and underfitting from excessive dropout; this study reports language-model results.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses dropout, batch-size effects and flatness in relation to generalization. Its own experiments vary dropout-mask samples with data minibatch size fixed and do not test the listed versions.

tranche.reason: The experiments concern dropout mechanisms and validation perplexity in language models, outside V6's fully connected and convolutional classifiers. No listed claim version is tested or used as a tool.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion paraphrase matches the text. The disappearance of implicit regularization on full WikiText-103 concerns dropout update noise; standard dropout still improves validation perplexity over the no-regularization baseline.
